title: NASA: Houston, We've Had a Problem
description: One explosion, one lifeboat, and a cardboard-and-plastic fix—NASA's most famous rescue in five steps.

questions.question: In April 1970, which NASA mission radioed home, "Houston, we've had a problem"?
questions.explanation: Jack Swigert said it first—"Okay, Houston, we've had a problem here"—and Jim Lovell repeated it. The crew was 200,000 miles out, headed for the Moon.

questions.question: Apollo 13's trouble started 56 hours in, when what blew up inside the service module?
questions.explanation: A routine stir of oxygen tank No. 2 sparked damaged wiring. The blast drained the fuel cells, and the command module was soon dying.

questions.question: With the oxygen tank gone and the command module powering down, the crew retreated into what lunar module?
questions.explanation: Built for two people for two days, Aquarius carried three for four. They shut down Odyssey to save its batteries for re-entry, and the cabin dropped to near freezing.

questions.question: Inside Aquarius, carbon dioxide kept rising. To fit square filters into round sockets, the crew taped up a fix using what?
questions.explanation: Engineers in Houston built the "mailbox" from only what was on board—duct tape, plastic bags, cardboard, a sock—then read the steps up to the crew.

questions.question: After the duct-tape fix got them home, Lovell's famous line was misquoted in the 1995 film—spoken by which actor?
questions.explanation: "Houston, we have a problem," Hanks says as Lovell. The real past tense, "we've had a problem," lost out to the movie's version, which is the one everyone quotes.

imageHint: A crippled spacecraft, three astronauts, and a long way home

questions.question: 'Failure is not an option' was written for the 1995 film Apollo 13—which flight director's character says it?
questions.hint: Played by Ed Harris, wearing a white vest

questions.question: NASA's Deep Space Network uses giant radio dishes to communicate with spacecraft. What is the diameter of the largest dishes?
questions.hint: About the length of a football field, these dishes can hear a whisper from billions of miles away
